title: Common Cold vs. Influenza
text: The common cold and influenza (flu) are both viral respiratory illnesses but differ in severity and symptom onset. Colds typically develop gradually with milder symptoms such as a runny nose, sore throat, and mild cough. The flu tends to come on more suddenly and severely, often including high fever, body aches, fatigue, and chills. Both are contagious and spread mainly through respiratory droplets; general prevention includes handwashing and, for flu, annual vaccination.
